reason: The description accurately captures all major stages of the parsing pipeline: TextUnmarshaler first, then custom funcMap parsers, then built-in kind-based parsers, then slice/map delegation, and finally a no-parser error. The pointer dereferencing behavior is correctly noted. The only minor gap is that the description doesn't mention the `.Convert(typee)` call applied when using built-in parsers (which handles named types based on basic kinds), but this is a secondary implementation detail that wouldn't block a correct reimplementation.
missing_functionality: When using built-in parsers, the parsed value is converted to the target type via reflect.Value.Convert(typee), which handles named types derived from basic kinds — this type conversion step is not mentioned.
incorrect_or_misleading_points: The description says pointer handling applies 'parsing to the pointed-to element type and stores the result in the underlying element', which is accurate, but it omits that the TextUnmarshaler check happens before the pointer unwrapping, meaning a pointer field that implements TextUnmarshaler is handled via that interface on the original (pointer) field, not the dereferenced element.
